row.Biography:
Bernard Andreae graduated from Marburg in 1956 under Friedrich Matz, specializing in Roman sarcophagi; his thesis analyzed historical motifs within sarcophagus iconography.
From 1956 to 1959, he served as Assistant at the German Archaeological Institute in Italy. In 1962, he completed his habilitation in Bonn with a monograph on Roman funerary art ("Studien zur roemischen Grabkunst"), dedicated to his mentors Friedrich Matz, Reinhard Herbig, and Ernst Langlotz.
Between 1960 and 1970, he published studies on painting and sculpture, including the Esquiline fresco cycle (1962), the Aldobrandini Wedding (1962), and imitation vs. originality in 3rd-century AD sarcophagi (1970).
In the 1970s and 1980s, he tracked the Rome Soprintendenza's excavations at Tiberius's Villa in Sperlonga, producing complex reconstructions of the Hellenistic-Roman sculpture groups. This work absorbed him during his tenure as professor at Bochum (1965-1977) and Marburg (from 1978), until his appointment as Director of the German Archaeological Institute in Rome in 1984 (until 1995).
His contributions to Neue Forschungen in Pompeji (1974) and a new edition of the Alexander Mosaic (1977) reflect his focus on Roman painting and Late Republican/Early Imperial classicism. This interest also drove his research at Hadrian's Villa and the Baiae excavations, where he served as scientific director for underwater research. On these themes, he published "Odysseus: Archäologie des europäischen Mythos" (1982: https://archive.org/details/laokoonunddiegru0000andr/page/n5/mode/2up ; Italian trans. "L’immagine di Ulisse", Einaudi 1983, trans. Giorgio Bejor), illustrating the mythic-cultural meaning of the Sperlonga group, and "Laokoon und die Gründung Roms" (1988; Italian trans. "Laocoonte e la fondazione di Roma", Il Saggiatore 1989).
Since 1974, he has edited the Roman sarcophagi corpus "Die antiken Sarkophagreliefs", authoring the 1980 volume on hunting scenes ("Die römischen Jagdsarkophage": https://digi.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/diglit/asr1_2 ).
